$comment: The collector's Apify rules (issue #926, parent #817): which actors a run may call, what each call may spend and return, which enrichments are forced off, and what one run may spend in total. apify-guard.mjs enforces every value here as a Claude Code PreToolUse hook, so the caps are code rather than Claude's obedience. Costs are unknown until the owner's bounded dry run (the issue's own open decision): the figures below are the pre-dry-run defaults, and the guard enforces whatever the owner puts here afterwards. Reaching a cap stops the run - the searches it did not reach are recorded as not_searched by the run completion (#937) - which is deliberately the failure mode rather than overspending. Monthly limits are account settings (Apify maxMonthlyUsageUsd and the Claude Console spend limit) and are not this file's business.

perRun.$comment: One collector run. 71 tracked products across the four Apify routes is roughly 350-400 calls with pagination, so 600 calls is a ceiling a normal run does not reach and a loop cannot pass. The charge cap counts the ceiling each call commits to rather than what Apify actually billed - the only figure a PreToolUse hook can know - so it is the worst case, never an estimate.

varnmill/au-supermarket-prices.$comment: Coles, Woolworths and ALDI. Keyword search is noisy ('kinder bueno' returned eggs in the owner's testing) and Claude filters it; products mode with prefixed ids (coles:5216969, woolworths:66527) is precise and is the fallback for a known listing missing from a day's search. onlyChanged is forced off because every listing must get a positive check (#925), and paid details are forced off because they are billed and nothing reads them.

abotapi/kmart-product-scraper.$comment: Kmart. Its keyword search is to be confirmed in the dry run (the issue says so). Reviews and local-stock enrichment are forced off: both are billed and neither is a price.

axlymxp/bigw-product-search.$comment: BIG W by name. Dromb's keyword search timed out in the owner's testing, so the name search is this actor's.

dromb/bigw-sku-lookup.$comment: BIG W by SKU, billed per start, and the fallback for a known listing missing from that day's name search - never the way a run searches by name. One page: a SKU lookup answers for the ids it was given.
